commands.review_summary:
The PR adds an image-tool guard that treats model-generated references such as `image_0` as prompt-visible images instead of filesystem paths.

PR surface: Source +19. Total +19 across 1 file.

Reproducibility: yes. from source: current main passes unschemed `image_0` into workspace-relative filesystem resolution, matching the linked reporter's v2026.6.11 failure; this review did not execute the live WebChat flow.

target.title: fix 'WebChat image attachments not mapped to media store path
target.body:
<!--

Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Required PR title:
type: user-facing description
Use a parenthesized scope only when it adds clarity:

Types: feat, fix, improve, refactor, docs, chore.
For fixes, describe the user-visible symptom and trigger:

Avoid implementation details such as:

Related: #103198
## What Problem This Solves
When a user sends an image attachment via WebChat, the assistant's image tool receives the reference image_0 which does not resolve to the actual file path in the media store (~/.openclaw/media/inbound/). The message says [User sent media without caption] but the image data is not accessible to the image tool.
<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
For fixes, begin with:
"Fixes an issue where users <do X> would <experience Y> when <condition>."
or:
"Resolves a problem where..."

Name the affected UI surface or workflow. Do not describe the code-level cause here.
-->

## Why This Change Was Made
  Added a regex check in src/agents/tools/image-tool.ts (line 944) that detects model-generated image index references
  (/^(?:image|img)[_\-:]?\d+$/i) before the classifyMediaReferenceSource check. When matched, it returns a helpful
  message telling the model that the image is already visible in the prompt and can be described directly —no
  filesystem access attempted.

  Patterns now caught:
  - image_0, image_1, ... (underscore —the reported bug)
  - image-0, image-1, ... (hyphen)
  - image:0, image:1, ... (colon —already caught by existing check, now gets a better message)
  - image0, image1, ... (no separator)
  - img_0, img-0, etc. (shorthand)
<!--
In one or two sentences, explain the complete shipped solution, key design
decisions, and relevant boundaries or non-goals. Include implementation detail
only when it helps reviewers understand user-visible behavior or risk.
Avoid file-by-file narration.
-->

## User Impact
  When a user sends an image attachment via WebChat without a caption, the assistant receives the image in its prompt
  context as inline base64 data. If the LLM then attempts to call the image tool to analyze that image, some models
  (notably Gemini) reference the image by a generated index label such as image_0. Because image_0 has no URI scheme and  no file extension, it passes through all existing validation gates and is resolved as a relative filesystem path
  (<workspace>/image_0), which does not exist. The tool fails with:

  ▎ Local media file not found

  The only workaround is for the user to manually provide a caption with the image or to avoid using the image tool on
  WebChat-attached images —neither of which is obvious to the user.

  After the fix, the tool detects these model-generated pseudo-references and returns a clear guidance message telling
  the model it can already see the image in the prompt, instead of crashing with a misleading filesystem error.
<!--
State what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect. Lead with the
concrete benefit and use user-facing language. If there is no user-visible
impact, say so plainly.
-->

## Evidence
  The existing guard in image-tool.ts:942 checks refInfo.hasUnsupportedScheme, which catches image:0 (the image: prefix
  is treated as an unrecognized URI scheme). However, image_0 uses an underscore instead of a colon —no scheme, no
  colon, so hasUnsupportedScheme returns false. The reference falls through to filesystem path resolution unchanged.

  Root cause

  // image-tool.ts line 942 (before fix) —only catches schemed patterns like "image:0"
  if (refInfo.hasUnsupportedScheme) { ... }

  // classifies image_0 →hasScheme: false, hasUnsupportedScheme: false
  // →treated as relative file path →<workspace>/image_0 →ENOENT
